question: Do season-long market lines, or the expert-vs-market disagreement, add anything on top of the shipped Sleeper -> VBD order? Built here as per-(player x season) features so that opp-lab.mjs can run them through the same grid, the same walk-forward and the same eight-placebo ceiling that rejected prevCarG.

variables.mktOwnHonest: Own implied team total, week 1 only (available before the draft)
variables.mktSosHonest: Mean over the full schedule of the opponent's week-1 implied points conceded
variables.mktPlayoffHonest: Same, weeks 15-17 only (the app shows this as Playoff D)
variables.mktOwnOracle: Own implied team total, all closing lines of the season (LEAKY - ceiling only)
variables.mktSosOracle: Mean over the schedule of the opponent's season-long implied points conceded (LEAKY)
variables.ecrVsAdp: adp - ecr. Positive: the experts are higher on him than the crowd
variables.ecrSd: Dispersion of the expert consensus about him

leak.oracleIsCeiling: mktOwnOracle / mktSosOracle / mktPlayoffOracle use closing lines from the whole season and are NOT a proposal. They are the ceiling: if the leaky version cannot beat the placebo family, no honest version can.
leak.honestCaveat: nflverse stores the CLOSING line, so even the week-1 line is set about two weeks after his draft. The honest arm is therefore optimistic, which is the safe direction for a null and the unsafe direction for a win.
leak.rosterTeam: Team comes from roster_{year}.csv, a season-level file. For a player traded in October it is the wrong team. Counted below, not assumed away.
